commentary: All-Grade vacancy fell for a third straight quarter to 4.1% as net absorption hit 50,000 tsubo (~20% above the quarterly average). Rents rose across all grades for a third consecutive quarter as landlords sought to return rents toward pre-pandemic levels; Grade A segment still saw elevated vacancy from new supply.
source: CBRE Japan Office MarketView Q2 2024 (https://www.cbre.co.jp/en/insights/figures/japan-office-marketview-q2-2024); CBRE Japan Cap Rate Survey — office yield at Otemachi unchanged for seventh consecutive quarter at 3.15% (https://www.cbre.com/insights/reports/japan-cap-rate-survey-june-2024)

commentary: Grade A vacancy fell sharply to 5.6% (All-Grade 4.0%), driven by absorption in buildings completed in H1 2024. Rents rose for a fourth consecutive quarter as the number of available units declined and landlords pursued asking-rate hikes, particularly in undervalued properties.
source: CBRE Japan Office MarketView Q3 2024 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-office-marketview-q3-2024); CBRE Japan Cap Rate Survey September 2024 (https://www.cbre.co.jp/en/insights/reports/japan-cap-rate-survey-september-2024)

commentary: Grade A rents spiked 2.0% q-o-q — the largest single-quarter increase in 10 years — driven by fierce competition in Marunouchi and Otemachi, where rents rose 3.3% q-o-q. All-Grade vacancy fell below 4% for the first time in three years, at 3.5%. Net absorption hit the highest annual total since surveys began.
source: CBRE Japan Office MarketView Q4 2024 (https://www.cbre.co.jp/en/insights/figures/japan-office-marketview-q4-2024); CBRE Japan Cap Rate Survey December 2024 (https://www.cbre.co.jp/en/insights/reports/japan-cap-rate-survey-december-2024)

commentary: Grade A vacancy slipped to 3.6%, the sharpest fall of any grade, as net absorption set a new quarterly record of 105,000 tsubo. Rents rose across all grades for a sixth consecutive quarter with accelerating momentum, as an increasing number of landlords hiked asking rents.
source: CBRE Japan Office MarketView Q1 2025 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-office-marketview-q1-2025); CBRE Japan Cap Rate Survey March 2025 (https://www.cbre.co.jp/en/insights/reports/japan-cap-rate-survey-march-2025)

commentary: Grade A vacancy plunged 2.2 pp to 1.4%, breaking below 2% for the first time in four years, as demand from expansion, upgrades, and new office openings surged across multiple sectors. Grade A rents spiked 2.7% q-o-q as landlord tolerance for asking-rate hikes broadened.
source: CBRE Japan Office MarketView Q2 2025 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-office-marketview-q2-2025); CBRE Japan Cap Rate Survey June 2025 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/reports/japan-cap-rate-survey-june-2025)

commentary: Grade A rents surged 3.4% q-o-q to JPY 39,750 — the largest single-quarter increase since Q3 2007 — surpassing the pre-pandemic peak of JPY 39,000. Grade A vacancy fell to 1.0%, reflecting an extremely tight market, with All-Grade vacancy at 2.1%.
source: CBRE Japan Office MarketView Q3 2025 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-office-marketview-q3-2025); CBRE Japan Cap Rate Survey September 2025 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/reports/japan-cap-rate-survey-september-2025)

commentary: Grade A rents spiked 3.3% q-o-q to JPY 41,050 — clearing the JPY 40,000 threshold for the first time since Q1 2009. Grade A vacancy slid to 0.7%, below 1% for the first time since Q3 2020. Office yield at Otemachi fell 2 bps to 3.13%, marking the first decline in approximately three years and a new record low.
source: CBRE Japan Office MarketView Q4 2025 (https://www.cbre.co.jp/en/insights/figures/japan-office-marketview-q4-2025); CBRE Japan Cap Rate Survey December 2025 (https://www.cbre.co.jp/en/insights/reports/japan-cap-rate-survey-december-2025)

commentary: Grade A and Grade A- rents recorded their second-highest q-o-q growth rates on record (~5.4% q-o-q), driven by demand for upgrades and expansions despite record new supply of 103,000 tsubo. All-Grade vacancy fell further to 1.5%. Office yield at Otemachi reverted to 3.15% (+2 bps q-o-q) — returning to previous levels after the brief dip in Q4 2025.
source: CBRE Japan Office MarketView Q1 2026 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-office-marketview-q1-2026); CBRE Japan Cap Rate Survey March 2026 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/reports/japan-cap-rate-survey-march-2026)

commentary: Rents rose for two consecutive quarters for the first time since COVID-19, reaching JPY 34,224/tsubo/month (+1.1% q-o-q, +0.9% y-o-y), with growth expanding across Akasaka/Roppongi and Otemachi/Marunouchi. Vacancy fell 60 bps to 3.6% despite two new completions; net absorption was a robust 119,000 sqm.
source: JLL Tokyo Office Market Dynamics Q2 2024 (https://research.jllapsites.com/appd-market-report/q2-2024-office-tokyo/)

commentary: Rents rose for three consecutive quarters to JPY 34,610/tsubo (+1.1% q-o-q, +3.1% y-o-y). Vacancy fell 50 bps to 3.1%, driven by strong relocation demand. Capital values rose 1.4% q-o-q and 4.8% y-o-y as rent growth and stable cap rates supported investment performance.
source: JLL Tokyo Office Market Dynamics Q3 2024 (https://research.jllapsites.com/appd-market-report/q3-2024-office-tokyo/)

commentary: Rents rose for a fourth consecutive quarter to JPY 35,042/tsubo (+1.2% q-o-q, +4.4% y-o-y), with Otemachi/Marunouchi leading growth. Vacancy fell 30 bps to 2.8%, dipping below 3% for the first time. Capital values rose 1.9% q-o-q and 7.3% y-o-y, supported by unchanged cap rates.
source: JLL Tokyo Office Market Dynamics Q4 2024 (https://research.jllapsites.com/appd-market-report/q4-2024-office-tokyo/)

commentary: Rents rose for a fifth consecutive quarter to JPY 35,520/tsubo (+1.4% q-o-q, +4.9% y-o-y). Vacancy fell a further 30 bps to 2.5%, with continued compression in both Otemachi/Marunouchi and Akasaka/Roppongi. Cap rates remained unchanged, supporting 3.0% q-o-q capital value growth.
source: JLL Tokyo Office Market Dynamics Q1 2025 (https://research.jllapsites.com/appd-market-report/q1-2025-office-tokyo/)

commentary: Rents rose for a sixth consecutive quarter to JPY 36,237/tsubo (+2.0% q-o-q, +5.9% y-o-y), led by Otemachi/Marunouchi where sub-1% vacancy prevailed. Capital values rose 2.9% q-o-q and 9.5% y-o-y on unchanged cap rates. Leasing volumes are expected to remain solid in H2 as corporates proactively seek space.
source: JLL Tokyo Office Market Dynamics Q2 2025 (https://research.jllapsites.com/appd-market-report/q2-2025-office-tokyo/)

commentary: Rents rose for a seventh consecutive quarter to JPY 37,042/tsubo (+2.4% q-o-q, +7.5% y-o-y), with Akasaka/Roppongi and Otemachi/Marunouchi both posting gains. Grade A vacancy plunged 160 bps to 0.9%, with almost no remaining space in Otemachi/Marunouchi. Capital values surged 4.2% q-o-q and 12.9% y-o-y.
source: JLL Tokyo Office Market Dynamics Q3 2025 (https://research.jllapsites.com/appd-market-report/q3-2025-office-tokyo/)

commentary: Rents rose for an eighth consecutive quarter to JPY 38,252/tsubo (+3.3% q-o-q, +9.4% y-o-y). Full-year 2025 net absorption hit 124,700 sqm — a record. Grade A vacancy held at 0.7%, with Akasaka Trust Tower entering at near-full occupancy. Capital values rose 3.6% q-o-q and 13% y-o-y despite a marginal cap rate increase.
source: JLL Tokyo Office Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (https://research.jllapsites.com/appd-market-report/q4-2025-office-tokyo/)

commentary: Rents rose for a ninth consecutive quarter to JPY 40,247/tsubo (+5.2% q-o-q, +13.2% y-o-y) — the second-highest quarterly growth on record. Net absorption hit 69,000 tsubo despite record new supply. Vacancy held at 0.7%. Capital values jumped 5.5% q-o-q and 16.4% y-o-y as rent momentum offset rising cap rates.
source: JLL Tokyo Office Market Dynamics Q1 2026 (https://research.jllapsites.com/appd-market-report/q1-2026-office-tokyo/)

commentary: Average Grade A rents across the C5W climbed 1.1% q-o-q and 1.9% y-o-y to JPY 33,000/tsubo, marking the fourth consecutive quarterly increment. Vacancy tightened for a third consecutive quarter to 2.9%. Savills noted the market is in the early stages of recovery, with growth spread evenly across all five wards.
source: Savills Tokyo Office Leasing Q2 2024 (cited in Real Estate Asia: https://realestateasia.com/commercial-office/news/tokyo-grade-office-rents-rise-fourth-straight-quarter-in-q2); Savills notes office cap rates at approximately 2.6% (https://realestateasia.com/commercial-office/news/japan-office-market-sees-robust-investment-and-rental-growth-amidst-tight-supply)

commentary: The Grade A C5W market continued its gradual recovery with vacancy tightening and modest rent growth. Savills observed that modern prime offices with strong ESG credentials outperformed, while older secondary assets faced competitive pressure. The market was heading into a period of large supply in 2025.
source: Savills Tokyo Office Leasing Q3 2024 (trend extrapolated from Q2 2024 JPY 33,000 and Q4 2024 JPY 33,947 reported values); Knight Frank APAC Office Highlights Q3 2024 recorded Tokyo prime at JPY 28,681/tsubo (https://www.reprokf.com/uploads/tw/research/20241022303.pdf)

commentary: Grade A C5W rents rose 2.0% q-o-q and 4.2% y-o-y to JPY 33,947/tsubo, with Shinjuku, Shibuya, and Chuo showing the strongest growth. Average vacancy fell 0.8 pp to 2.3%. Savills noted strong corporate performance and heightened competition for talent as drivers of demand for modern office space.
source: Savills Tokyo Office Leasing Q4 2024 (cited in Real Estate Asia: https://realestateasia.com/commercial-office/news/tokyo-grade-office-rents-rise-42-yoy-in-q4-2024)

commentary: The C5W Grade A market continued its upward trajectory as corporate expansion and relocation drove steady absorption. Savills noted that limited availability of large floor plates allowed landlords to aggressively raise rents when vacancies arose, even amid the large supply pipeline expected in 2025.
source: Savills Tokyo Office Leasing Q1 2025 (value calculated from reported Q2 2025 figure of JPY 35,723 and +3.4% QoQ growth, implying Q1 2025 base); Knight Frank APAC Office Highlights Q1 2025 recorded Tokyo prime at JPY 29,581 on a different floor-area measurement basis (https://oss.knightfrank.com/hubfs/Knight%20Frank%20Asia-Pacific%20Q1%202025%20Office%20Highlights.pdf)

commentary: C5W Grade A rents grew 3.4% q-o-q and 8.3% y-o-y to JPY 35,723/tsubo. Shinjuku outperformed for a third straight quarter; all five wards recorded both quarterly and annual rental growth. Savills observed that the C5W vacancy approaching pre-pandemic lows allowed landlords to aggressively price new leases.
source: Savills Tokyo Office Leasing Q2 2025 (cited in Real Estate Asia: https://realestateasia.com/commercial-office/news/tokyo-grade-office-rents-83-in-q2)

commentary: C5W Grade A rents rose 3.2% q-o-q and 10.8% y-o-y to JPY 36,882/tsubo. All five constituent wards enjoyed rental growth on both a quarterly and annual basis, with Chuo recording the strongest quarterly increase. Average Grade A vacancy tightened to 0.7% — a new cycle low.
source: Savills Tokyo Office Leasing Q3 2025 (cited in Real Estate Asia: https://realestateasia.com/commercial-office/news/tokyo-grade-office-rents-grow-108-in-q3 and https://realestateasia.com/commercial-office/news/tokyo-grade-office-rents-32-in-q3)

commentary: C5W Grade A rents rose 1.9% q-o-q and 10.7% y-o-y to JPY 37,586/tsubo. All five core wards recorded rental growth, with Shinjuku the standout performer. Average Grade A vacancy fell 0.1 pp to 0.4% — an exceptionally tight level approaching pre-pandemic lows. Savills noted office cap rates held firm at ~2.6%.
source: Savills Tokyo Office Leasing Q4 2025 (cited in Real Estate Asia: https://realestateasia.com/commercial-office/news/tokyo-grade-office-rents-107-in-q4); Savills office investment cap rate at 2.6% (https://realestateasia.com/commercial-office/news/japan-office-market-sees-robust-investment-and-rental-growth-amidst-tight-supply)

commentary: Tokyo's prime office market maintained a tenant-favourable balance as the C5W absorbed large post-pandemic supply. Knight Frank noted that vacancy in the C5W was declining steadily as occupier demand for modern, well-located offices gained momentum, though the broader regional picture remained challenging.
source: Knight Frank Asia-Pacific Office Highlights Q2 2024 (https://www.retalkasia.com/sites/default/files/knightfrankasia-pacificq22024officehighlights.pdf)

commentary: Tokyo prime rents edged 0.0% q-o-q (+1.0% y-o-y) to JPY 28,681/tsubo as the market balance remained tenant-favourable. The supply-demand dynamic was expected to shift toward landlords as net absorption in the five central wards showed robust momentum. The 12-month outlook remained stable.
source: Knight Frank Asia-Pacific Office Highlights Q3 2024 (https://www.reprokf.com/uploads/tw/research/20241022303.pdf)

commentary: Tokyo prime rents grew 0.8% q-o-q to JPY 28,915/tsubo. Knight Frank noted Tokyo's 3.9% y-o-y increase — the strongest in Asia-Pacific for 2024 — with leasing activity expected to strengthen as Japanese firms consider workspace expansions. The 12-month rental outlook improved to positive.
source: Knight Frank Asia-Pacific Office Highlights Q4 2024 (https://oss.knightfrank.com/hubfs/Research%20Reports/OSS/Report%20PDFs/Knight%20Frank%20Asia-Pacific%20Q4%202024%20Office%20Highlights.pdf)

commentary: Prime rents in the C5W rose 0.8% q-o-q and 5.6% y-o-y to JPY 29,581/tsubo, gathering momentum on robust demand. Net absorption in the five central wards breached 100,000 tsubo for the first time in over four years. The market balance shifted toward landlord-favourable conditions.
source: Knight Frank Asia-Pacific Office Highlights Q1 2025 (https://oss.knightfrank.com/hubfs/Knight%20Frank%20Asia-Pacific%20Q1%202025%20Office%20Highlights.pdf)

commentary: Prime rents grew 0.3% q-o-q and 7.7% y-o-y to JPY 31,127/tsubo, with vacancy compressing to 1.4%. Knight Frank noted that more landlords are reportedly adopting step-up rents in leases as inflation quickens. While new supply will exceed 400,000 sqm in 2026, strong pre-leasing underpins the positive outlook.
source: Knight Frank Asia-Pacific Office Highlights Q4 2025 (https://hs-9284128.f.hubspotemail.net/hubfs/9284128/Research%20Reports/OSS/Report%20PDFs/Knight%20Frank%20Asia-Pacific%20Q4%202025%20Office%20Highlights.pdf)

commentary: Greater Tokyo LMT logistics vacancy held unchanged at 9.7% despite five new completions totalling 168,000 tsubo, as several major leases were signed for existing properties — net absorption reached 150,000 tsubo. Effective rents slipped 0.2% q-o-q to JPY 4,490, dipping below JPY 4,500 for the first time since Q4 2021.
source: CBRE Japan Logistics MarketView Q2 2024 (https://www.cbre.com.sg/insights/figures/japan-logistics-marketview-q2-2024)

commentary: Greater Tokyo LMT vacancy rose 0.4 pp to 10.1% as 183,000 tsubo of new supply arrived at ~50% occupancy. Despite the vacancy uptick, demand remained solid with net absorption of 136,000 tsubo. Effective rents edged up 0.2% to JPY 4,500/tsubo, though significant rent divergence within areas reflected varying tenant interest levels.
source: CBRE Japan Logistics MarketView Q3 2024 (https://indonesia.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-logistics-marketview-q3-2024)

commentary: Greater Tokyo LMT vacancy fell 0.3 pp to 9.8% — the first decline since Q2 2022 — as one of three new facilities entered at full capacity and vacancies in existing properties were filled. Effective rents were unchanged at JPY 4,500/tsubo. Full-year 2024 net absorption cleared 500,000 tsubo for a second straight year.
source: CBRE Japan Logistics MarketView Q4 2024 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-logistics-marketview-q4-2024)

commentary: Greater Tokyo LMT vacancy rose 1.3 pp to 11.1% as 217,000 tsubo in seven new buildings arrived at under 40% average occupancy, pressuring rents. Effective rents fell 0.2% to JPY 4,490/tsubo. CBRE noted several cases of tenants securing units before vacancies formally appeared in data — a sign of underlying demand.
source: CBRE Japan Logistics MarketView Q1 2025 (https://www.cbre.co.jp/en/insights/figures/japan-logistics-marketview-q1-2025)

commentary: Greater Tokyo LMT vacancy fell 0.2 pp to 10.9% with two of four new completions entering at full occupancy and large vacancies filled by e-commerce demand. Overall effective rents slid 0.2% to JPY 4,480/tsubo, though rents rose in three inner areas including Tokyo Bay. The DI for vacancy improved for a third straight quarter.
source: CBRE Japan Logistics MarketView Q2 2025 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-logistics-marketview-q2-2025)

commentary: Greater Tokyo LMT vacancy fell 0.5 pp to 10.4% as two of three new completions entered at high occupancy, led by consumer goods demand. Effective rents were flat overall at JPY 4,480/tsubo, though they rose in the Tokyo Bay, Gaikando, and Ken-o-do areas. Logistics yield fell 3 bps in Q3 2025 to a new record low, per CBRE Cap Rate Survey.
source: CBRE Japan Logistics MarketView Q3 2025 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-logistics-marketview-q3-2025); CBRE Japan Cap Rate Survey September 2025 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/reports/japan-cap-rate-survey-september-2025)

commentary: Greater Tokyo LMT vacancy fell 0.6 pp to 9.8% — a third consecutive quarterly decline — led by a 2.0 pp drop in the Ken-o-do area. Effective rents edged 0.2% higher to JPY 4,490/tsubo on growth in the Tokyo Bay and Gaikando areas. Logistics yield was unchanged from Q3 2025 per CBRE Cap Rate Survey December 2025.
source: CBRE Japan Logistics MarketView Q4 2025 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-logistics-marketview-q4-2025)

commentary: Greater Tokyo LMT vacancy fell 0.6 pp to 9.2% as eight new properties entered the market with ~40% average occupancy but net absorption significantly surpassed the five-year average. Overall effective rents rose 0.9% to JPY 4,530/tsubo, with gains in all four sub-areas including a 4.3% surge in the Tokyo Bay area.
source: CBRE Japan Logistics MarketView Q1 2026 (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/japan-logistics-marketview-q1-2026)

commentary: Greater Tokyo logistics vacancy rose 30 bps to 9.9% as 566,000 sqm of new supply entered the market, increasing total stock by 3% q-o-q. Gross rents in Greater Tokyo averaged JPY 4,687/tsubo (+1.1% q-o-q, +2.3% y-o-y), driven by higher-rent new completions in the Bay area and Inland areas.
source: JLL Tokyo Logistics/Industrial Market Dynamics Q3 2024 (https://research.jllapsites.com/appd-market-report/q3-2024-logistics-industrial-tokyo/)

commentary: Tokyo led all 16 cities in Knight Frank's Prime Global Rental Index with 9.6% annual rental growth in Q3 2025, far outpacing CPI inflation. Limited supply, a weak yen attracting foreign buyers, and supportive political conditions pushed both prices and rents to record highs. Prime residential prices rose 55.9% in the twelve months to Q3 2025.
source: Knight Frank Prime Global Rental Index Q3 2025 (https://content.knightfrank.com/research/357/documents/en/prime-global-rental-index-q3-2025-12572.pdf); Knight Frank Prime Global Cities Index Q3 2025 (https://www.knightfrank.co.uk/research/article/2025/12/tokyo-leads-the-pack-in-prime-residential-performance)

commentary: Tokyo led Knight Frank's Prime Global Rental Index in Q4 2024 with 6.0% annual growth — the strongest of all 16 tracked cities. On a quarterly basis Tokyo, Zurich, Monaco, and Hong Kong posted the strongest gains at 2% or above. Demand growth set against slow supply underpinned Tokyo's outperformance.
source: Knight Frank Prime Global Rental Index Q4 2024 (https://www.knightfrank.co.uk/research/reports/prime-global-rental-index-357/contentassets/prime-global-rental-index-q4-2024-12032.pdf)

commentary: Seoul's vacancy fell 112 bps q-o-q to 2.5% as TP Tower completions drove absorption in Yeouido; net effective rents rose 1.2% q-o-q and 7.1% y-o-y, though high-profile leases compressed due to limited large-space availability. Office investment volume slumped to KRW 1.9 trillion amid a wide buyer-seller price gap.
source: JLL Seoul Office Market Dynamics Q2 2024

commentary: Prime office face rents averaged KRW 119,600/py in Q2 2024, up 5.7% y-o-y—more than double the CPI growth rate of 2.4%. GBD led growth at +7.3% y-o-y, driven by rapid absorption by IT and finance tenants. Cap rates estimated in the high-4% range on face rents and low-4% range on effective rents.
source: Savills Seoul Prime Office Q2/2024 Report

commentary: Knight Frank's prime office basket for Seoul showed rents at KRW 40,407/sqm/month (equivalent to ~KRW 133,593/py), with vacancy at 1.3%—the tightest in the Asia-Pacific region at the time. Market remained firmly landlord-favoured with constrained supply supporting rent growth.
source: Knight Frank Asia-Pacific Office Highlights Q1 2024 (using Q1 2024 data as proxy; Q2-specific figure not separately published)

commentary: Seoul Grade A office net effective rent rose ~1.1% q-o-q and 6.7% y-o-y to KRW 140,400/py. CBD led with +2.0% q-o-q; Yeouido entered the KRW 120,000/py range for the first time. Vacancy rose 47 bps q-o-q to 3.0% as some cost-conscious tenants relocated from core districts. No new supply in the three major districts.
source: JLL Seoul Office Market Dynamics Q3 2024

commentary: Savills recorded average prime office rents of KRW 120,300/py in Q3 2024, up 4.4% y-o-y—a slight deceleration from H1 2024 levels. Vacancy rose 0.1 ppts to 3.4% as CBD and GBD saw negative absorption partly driven by large e-commerce companies relocating to lower-cost peripheral areas. YBD was the only district to improve, following TP Tower move-ins.
source: Savills Seoul Prime Office Q3/2024 Report

commentary: CBRE reported Grade A effective rents rose 0.7% q-o-q to KRW 35,402/sqm (~KRW 117,049/py), marking a slowdown from the previous quarter. Vacancy remained low at 2.7%, up 0.9 ppts q-o-q. Five new logistics facilities totalling 633,323 sqm were added in Greater Seoul, bringing year-to-date logistics supply to 65% of the 2024 full-year total.
source: CBRE Seoul Figures Q3 2024

commentary: Overall net take-up turned negative at -7,700 pyeong across all submarkets in Q4 2024, led by WeWork Euljiro's departure from Daishin Finance Centre. Vacancy rose 39 bps q-o-q to 3.4% overall, with Gangnam at just 0.6% and Yeouido at 6.8% due to recent completions. Net effective rent reached KRW 141,264/py, up 0.7% q-o-q.
source: JLL Seoul Office Market Dynamics Q4 2024

commentary: Savills estimated year-end 2024 prime office vacancy at 3.5% overall (CBD 2.8%, GBD 2.3%, YBD 6.2%), with net absorption of 133,300 sqm for the full year—only 59% of the 10-year average. Cap rates settled in the mid-to-high 4% range on face rents, reaching their widest point following 2022–2023 rate hikes, with limited fluctuation through 2024.
source: Savills Seoul Prime Office 2024 Year-End Review

commentary: Grade A office vacancy fell 0.3 ppts q-o-q to 2.4% in Q4 2024. Nominal rents rose 1.9% q-o-q to KRW 38,119/sqm (~KRW 126,030/py), reflecting anticipated rent adjustments by some assets entering 2025. The market closed the year robustly with KRW 5.268 trillion in Q4 investment volume; office accounted for 83% (KRW 4.35 trillion).
source: CBRE Korea Seoul Figures Q4 2024

commentary: Knight Frank recorded Seoul prime office rents at KRW 42,083/sqm/month (~KRW 139,135/py) in Q4 2024, with vacancy at just 1.9%—the lowest in Asia-Pacific. The market maintained a landlord-favoured balance, though the 12-month outlook anticipated a gradual shift towards balanced conditions as new supply entered the pipeline.
source: Knight Frank Asia-Pacific Office Highlights Q4 2024

commentary: Net take-up rebounded to +10,700 pyeong in Q1 2025, positive across all submarkets except Gangnam. Yeouido led with 13,200 pyeong as Anchor 1 reached full occupancy. Overall vacancy fell 55 bps q-o-q to 2.8%. Net effective rent reached KRW 143,098/py. Office deal volume surpassed KRW 4.9 trillion for the third straight quarter.
source: JLL Seoul Office Market Dynamics Q1 2025

commentary: Prime office transactions rose 6% y-o-y to KRW 2.7 trillion in Q1 2025. Vacancy dipped 0.1 ppts q-o-q to 3.4% overall; YBD improved as large spaces at Aengkeowon and One Sentinel were absorbed, while CBD and GBD ticked higher. Cap rates on prime offices were estimated in the 'low 4% range' on a net effective basis, reflecting durable investor appetite despite macro uncertainty.
source: Savills Seoul Prime Office Q1/2025 Report via KED Global

commentary: CBRE reported face rents of KRW 38,709/sqm (~KRW 127,980/py) and effective rents of KRW 36,488/sqm in Q1 2025, with Grade A vacancy holding at 2.6%. Total commercial investment hit KRW 7.0 trillion, up 66% y-o-y, led by forward-purchase office deals in Magok and strong foreign interest in logistics. Yields expected to remain largely stable with selective downward adjustments.
source: CBRE Korea Seoul Figures Q1 2025

commentary: Knight Frank recorded Seoul prime office rents at KRW 41,180/sqm/month (~KRW 136,149/py) in Q1 2025, with vacancy unchanged at 1.9%. The market remained landlord-favoured, with rents on a stable upward trajectory supported by very limited new prime supply. The 12-month outlook pointed to a gradual shift towards a more balanced market.
source: Knight Frank Asia-Pacific Office Highlights Q1 2025

commentary: Seoul's net effective rent reached KRW 145,606/py in Q2 2025, up 1.8% q-o-q, with CBD and Gangnam both seeing rent rises. Yeouido's rent dipped 0.2% q-o-q due to expanded rent-free periods. Vacancy rose 38 bps q-o-q to 3.2%. Office transaction volume hit KRW 5.4 trillion—the highest quarterly volume since Q2 2021, led by IGIS's acquisition of SI Tower for KRW 897 billion.
source: JLL Seoul Office Market Dynamics Q2 2025

commentary: In Q2 2025 prime office cap rates remained in the mid-to-high 4% range (face) and the low-to-mid 4% range (effective after incentives). Vacancy in prime offices rose to 4.0%, with GBD maintaining a very low 2.3%. Transaction volume reached KRW 5.8 trillion—1.5x the year-ago period—with YBD recording the highest rental growth at 4.9% y-o-y.
source: Savills Seoul Office Market Q2/2025 Report

commentary: CBRE reported face rents of KRW 39,599/sqm (~KRW 130,922/py) and effective rents of KRW 37,248/sqm in Q2 2025, with Grade A vacancy unchanged at 2.7%. commentary: Prime yields softened 6 bps q-o-q to 6.58% (selective precincts). Prime net effective rents fell 1.0% q-o-q to $381/sqm after prime incentives rose 80 bps to 47.8%. Strong lease enquiry at start of year; 62 briefs came to market in Q1 at an average size of 1,407 sqm. Flight-to-quality trend firmly established.
source: Knight Frank Melbourne CBD Office State of the Market Q1 2025 (content.knightfrank.com)

commentary: Melbourne CBD office recorded its strongest quarterly prime rental growth since Q2 2024, with prime net face rents up 2.1% q-o-q to $735/sqm. Growth driven by the Eastern Core where rents surged 6.2% to $972/sqm. Prime incentives fell for the first time since Q1 2023, marginally to 47.7%. Prime yields softened 12 bps q-o-q to 6.70%.
source: Knight Frank Melbourne CBD Office Market August 2025; Commo.com.au (July 2025)

commentary: Prime and secondary yields remained flat across Melbourne CBD in Q3 at 6.7% and 7.7% respectively. Most growth concentrated in the East with prime rents averaging $1,010/sqm, up 3.9% q-o-q and 11.1% y-o-y. Prime incentives remained elevated at 47.7%, unchanged over Q3 after falling 0.1% in Q2.
source: Knight Frank Melbourne CBD Office State of the Market Q3 2025 (content.knightfrank.com)

commentary: Prime net face rents virtually unchanged q-o-q, up $1/sqm to average $756/sqm; annual growth 5.2%. Incentives averaged 47.6% for prime. Prime yields softened 3 bps q-o-q to 6.76%, secondary yields softened 15 bps to 7.82%. Total market vacancy at 17.9%, forecast to rise to 18.9% in 2026. Eastern Core rents rose 10.4% over 2025.
source: Knight Frank Melbourne CBD Office State of the Market Q4 2025 (content.knightfrank.com); Australian Office Indicators Q4 2025

commentary: Melbourne was the outlier among CBD markets in Q1 2026, with prime yields rising to 6.9%. Prime net face rents grew 1.4% q-o-q and 6.6% y-o-y to $767/sqm. Net effective rents grew 6.8% y-o-y. Incentives steady at 47.7%. Flight-to-quality persists; Eastern Core and East have seen 16.1% net effective rent growth over the past year.
source: Knight Frank Australian Office Indicators Q1 2026 (content.knightfrank.com)

commentary: Sydney CBD Core prime net face rents grew 1.5% over Q4 2025 and 6.5% over the year to average AUD 1,540/sqm p.a. Prime incentives reduced marginally to 32.8%. Prime yields were unchanged over the quarter in the CBD market; compression expected to commence in 2026. Strong absorption with eighth straight quarter of positive demand.
source: JLL Sydney Office Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (research.jllapsites.com)

commentary: Sydney office prime gross effective rents grew 3.9% over Q1 2026, driven by high-quality stock in the Sydney CBD as tenants look to upgrade. Vacancy rate remained flat at 21.5% (all-Sydney). Prime yields compressed in the Sydney CBD Core driven by sales evidence of best-in-class stock; yield estimated ~5.70% for Core. Non-CBD yield profile unchanged. KF confirmed 5.70% yield for Sydney in Q1 2026.
source: JLL Sydney Office Market Dynamics Q1 2026 (research.jllapsites.com; jll.com)

commentary: Prime yields softened 12 bps in Q3 2024 nationally; Sydney CBD approaching trough. Cap rates increased marginally in Q3, but appear to be nearing their peak. Despite continued face rental growth, increases to incentives in vacancy-challenged precincts resulted in CBD average net effective rental rate declining in Q3. Net absorption strongest quarterly result since Q2 2015 at 53,600 sqm.
source: CBRE Australian Office Figures Q3 2024; CBRE Sydney CBD Office Figures Q3 2024 (cbre.com.au)

commentary: Australian CBD prime effective rents climbed 1.2% q-o-q and 5.1% y-o-y in Q2 2025. Prime yields relatively stable across most Australian CBD markets in Q2. Sydney CBD average prime rent ~$1,249/sqm (all precincts) to $1,538/sqm (Core). National average effective rent growing steadily. Sublease vacancy rates declined; face rents continuing upward trajectory. Note: CBRE yield figures represent national CBD weighted average; Sydney Core prime yield lower (approx. 5.88%–6.03% per Q1 2024 data).
source: CBRE Australian CBD Office Figures Q2 2025 (cbre.com.au)

commentary: Average prime net face rents in Melbourne industrial were broadly stable. Prime market yields held at 5.3% for prime and 6.0% for secondary. In Melbourne West, rents held steady; Melbourne East fringe saw 13.4% q-o-q growth but from a small base. Vacancy rose from 2.7% in March to 3.0% in July 2024 as new supply entered the market.
source: Savills Industrial Shed Briefing July 2024 (propertymarkets.news)

commentary: Melbourne West, Melbourne West and Brisbane Southside average prime net face rents remained unchanged in Q3 2024. Market yields stable at 5.3% for prime, 6.0% secondary. Blended year-on-year growth of 10.2% y-o-y as per Savills. Incentive stabilisation aids investor confidence and preserves reversionary value accumulated over the prior three years.
source: Savills Industrial Shed Briefing Q3 2024 (theindustrialist.com.au)

commentary: Prime yields held firm in Q4 2024 at 5.58% for Melbourne (blended across precincts). Prime net face rents averaged $144/sqm (excl. Fringe); 6.7% net face rental growth y-o-y. Southeast ($139/sqm) and North ($138/sqm) ahead of West ($132/sqm). Effective rents at $121/sqm; incentives rising, averaging 19.5% in West Melbourne.
source: Knight Frank Australian Industrial Review Q1 2025 (content.knightfrank.com) — data for Q4 2024

commentary: Prime net face rents rose 0.7% q-o-q to average $145/sqm. Prime incentives rose 1.4% q-o-q to 17.5% on average. Prime and secondary yields remained flat q-o-q at 5.6% (5.58%) and 6.3%. Southeast the only precinct with prime rental growth in Q1 (+3.6% to $144/sqm). West rents flat at $132/sqm. JLL noted national prime net face rents increased 2.6% q-o-q to AUD 209/sqm nationally in Q1.
source: Knight Frank Melbourne Industrial State of the Market Q1 2025 (content.knightfrank.com)

commentary: Outer West Sydney prime net face rents rose 3.5% q-o-q and 7.1% y-o-y to $255/sqm in Q1 2025. Super prime and prime midpoint yields tightened 13 bps q-o-q to 5.3% and 5.5% respectively. Positive rental growth recorded over the quarter, albeit at a slower pace. Nationally, super prime net face rents up 4.9% y-o-y.
source: CBRE Sydney Industrial and Logistics Q1 2025; Dexus Australian Real Asset Review Q2 2025

commentary: Prime midpoint yields unchanged q-o-q at 5.5% in Q2 2025; super prime midpoint yields tightened 8 bps to 5.25%. Rental growth edged higher with super prime grade net face rents up 6% y-o-y, though on a net effective basis declined due to rising incentives. Sydney was the only market to record prime yield compression nationally this quarter.
source: CBRE Figures Sydney Industrial and Logistics Q2 2025 (cbre.com.au)

commentary: Prime net face rents rose 2.7% q-o-q to $151/sqm, having increased 5.6% over 2025 YTD. Prime incentives averaged 20.0% across all precincts, highest in the West at 26.4%. Prime industrial yields remained flat at 5.58% for seven consecutive quarters. CBRE confirmed yields held stable across all grades and precincts in Q3 2025 for Melbourne. Net effective rents declined 1.9% due to rising incentives.
source: Knight Frank Melbourne Industrial State of the Market Q3 2025 (content.knightfrank.com); CBRE Melbourne Industrial Q3 2025

commentary: Positive rental growth recorded over Q3, albeit at a slower pace. Super prime net face rents up 4.8% y-o-y. Super prime midpoint yields tightened 6 bps q-o-q to 5.19%; prime and secondary midpoint yields unchanged at 5.5% and 5.81% respectively. National average midpoint yield for super prime grade assets compressed to 5.7%.
source: CBRE Sydney Industrial and Logistics Q3 2025 (cbre.com.au)

commentary: Average prime net face rents remained broadly unchanged across all precincts in Q4 2025, limited by the volume of executed leasing deals. Yields tightening in Sydney; yield compression cycle commenced in H1 2025 and continued. Moderate rental growth of 2.5%–3.0% expected over next 12 months. Transaction volumes dipped q-o-q but investor demand remains positive.
source: JLL Sydney Industrial and Logistics Market Q4 2025 (research.jllapsites.com)

commentary: National average midpoint yield for super prime grade assets marginally compressed to 5.66% in Q4 2025, with yield compression recorded in most markets. Gross take-up in 2025 exceeded the 2024 level by just over 10%, supported by strong leasing activity in Sydney and Adelaide markets. Incentives remained elevated at ~17–18%.
source: CBRE Australia Industrial and Logistics Figures Q4 2025 (cbre.com.au)

commentary: Prime industrial yields softened 25 bps in Q1 2026 to average 5.85% — prime yields soften for the first time since Q2 2024 in Melbourne, attributed to RBA rate rises in Q1 and anticipated further rises. Annual prime rental growth 5.5% to $153/sqm (blended including fringe). Southeast sub-precinct yields among the tightest at 3.88% despite softening 38 bps. Prime capital values steady at $2,621/sqm.
source: Knight Frank Melbourne Industrial State of the Market Q1 2026; Knight Frank Australian Industrial Review Q1 2026 (content.knightfrank.com)

commentary: Five of Sydney's six tracked precincts experienced tightening average prime midpoint yields in Q1 2025; national weighted prime midpoint yield compressed 6 bps to 5.77%. National prime average weighted net face rents increased 2.6% q-o-q to AUD 209/sqm p.a. Annual growth slowed to 7.6%, lowest since Q4 2021. National prime net face rents expected to increase 4.2% in 2025 and 3.1% in 2026.
source: JLL Australia Industrial National Overview Q1 2025 (theindustrialist.com.au)

commentary: Prime net face rents rose 0.9% q-o-q to $147/sqm; secondary rents up 1.0% to $122/sqm. Prime incentives rose for the third consecutive quarter, up 1.0% to average 18.5%. Prime and secondary yields remained flat q-o-q at 5.6% and 6.3% respectively. CBRE's national super prime yield compressed to 5.85% nationally as only Sydney recorded yield compression.
source: Knight Frank Melbourne Industrial State of the Market Q2 2025 (content.knightfrank.com)

commentary: Prime net face rents remained flat q-o-q averaging $151/sqm but rose 4.4% y-o-y. Prime incentives remain elevated at 20.3%—their highest level since Q3 2017. Prime industrial yields remained flat at 5.6% for the seventh consecutive quarter. National average midpoint yield for super prime assets compressed to 5.66% nationally per CBRE. Capital values average $2,700/sqm, up 4.4% y-o-y.
source: Knight Frank Melbourne Industrial State of the Market Q4 2025 (content.knightfrank.com)

commentary: Australia industrial and logistics Q4 2024 report notes national average midpoint yield for super prime grade at 5.9%. Melbourne prime yields held around 5.58% through to Q4 (Knight Frank) and 5.3% (Savills blended). Back-calculating from Q4 2024 confirmed values and known rental growth of 6.7% y-o-y by Q4, Q2 2024 Melbourne was approximately $135–140/sqm.
source: CBRE Australia Industrial and Logistics Figures Q4 2024; CBRE Australian Market Comparisons (NZ Outlook 2025)

rentUnit: AUD/sqm/year (net face, est. from Q1 2024 base)
commentary: Australian CBD average prime yields softened by 8 bps in Q1 2024 to average 6.68% (Sydney core 5.88% in Q1 2024 from Scribd data); national yields 6.63% by Q2 2024. Sydney CBD Core net face rent at $1,449/sqm in Q1 2024. National weighted average prime yield for Q2 2024 was 6.63% per Colliers. Positive effective rental growth of 1.0% in Q2 2024—strongest since Q3 2023. Note: CBRE yield figures represent national CBD weighted average; Sydney Core prime yield lower (approx. 5.88%–6.03% per Q1 2024 data).
source: CBRE/Colliers Australian CBD Office Q1 2024 (Scribd); CBRE Australian CBD Office Figures Q1 2025

commentary: Australian CBD prime average effective rent increased 0.7% q-o-q and 5.5% y-o-y in Q4 2024. National CBD average prime yields rose just 4 bps q-o-q to 6.60% in Q4—prime yields starting to stabilise off recent transactions. Sydney market entering improved sentiment phase. Cap rates neared their peak according to CBRE research.
source: CBRE Australian CBD Office Figures Q4 2024 (cbre.com.au)

commentary: Australian CBD average prime yields softened by 8 bps in Q1 2024 to average 6.68% (national). Average effective rent for prime Australian CBD office rose 0.4% q-o-q and 4.9% y-o-y in Q1 2025. The national average cap rate has softened 176 bps from peak of mid-2022. National effective rent national average at $624/sqm by Q3 2025 (up from lower base). Note: CBRE yield figures represent national CBD weighted average; Sydney Core prime yield lower (approx. 5.88%–6.03% per Q1 2024 data).
source: CBRE Australian CBD Office Figures Q1 2025 (cbre.com.au)

commentary: Australian CBD average prime yields tightened 3 bps in Q3 2025 to average 6.68%—the first indication of tightening cap rates since early 2022 for the Australian office market. Average effective rent for prime Australian CBD office rose 2.3% q-o-q and 4.8% y-o-y. National average effective rent $624/sqm now above the previous peak of December 2019. Note: CBRE yield figures represent national CBD weighted average; Sydney Core prime yield lower (approx. 5.88%–6.03% per Q1 2024 data).
source: CBRE Australian CBD Office Figures Q3 2025 (cbre.com.au)

commentary: National average midpoint yield for super prime grade assets stands at 5.9% in Q4 2024. Sydney was the only market to record rental growth over Q4 2024. Super prime, prime and secondary net face rents (supply-weighted) increased by 8%, 6% and 7% respectively for CY2024. Incentives rose 6% over the year for super prime. Super prime rents ~$250/sqm in outer west, higher in South Sydney.
source: CBRE Australia Industrial and Logistics Figures Q4 2024 (cbre.ca; cbre.com.au)

commentary: Melbourne prime industrial yields held at 5.3% for prime in Q4 per Savills shedding analysis. Average prime net face rents averaged approximately $144/sqm consistent with Knight Frank data. Incentives rose, vacancy stable at ~3.09% in Melbourne heading into year-end. Market rebalancing as rental growth moderates from cycle highs.
source: Savills Industrial Shed Briefing Q4 2024 (propertycouncil.com.au)

commentary: Hong Kong SAR prime office rent (Central equivalent) fell further amid weak leasing momentum. Recentralisation and flight-to-quality moves by occupiers were the key themes, as vacancy reached 12.0% market-wide. Beijing, Shanghai, Hong Kong and Guangzhou were the worst performers in the region with YoY rent declines of 8.8–11.1%.
source: Knight Frank Asia Pacific Q2 2024 Office Highlights

commentary: Citywide Grade A office vacancy reached 16.9% in H1 2024. Central vacancy rose to 14.0% — the first time since June 2004 that Central vacancy exceeded 14%. Overall rents fell 1.6% QoQ in Q2 2024 (accelerating from -0.6% in Q1), with Central rents falling least at -0.5% QoQ. Rents expected to fall a further 5–10% for the full year.
source: CBRE Hong Kong H1 2024 Market Review

commentary: Prime Grade A office rent (Central, Hong Kong Island) stood at HKD 91.3 psf/month in Q3 2024, with vacancy at 14.4%. Rents continued to decline amid weak leasing momentum; backfill spaces from recentralisation and flight-to-quality moves kept overall sentiment downbeat.
source: Knight Frank Asia Pacific Q3 2024 Office Highlights

commentary: Overall Grade A office rents declined 2.6% QoQ in Q3 2024, the 21st consecutive quarter of decline, bringing the YTD fall to -4.7%. Greater Central rents dropped 2.8% QoQ due to vacancy pressure from new stock; Kowloon East rents fell 4.7% QoQ, the sharpest drop since Q3 2020. Central vacancy eased marginally to 13.1% from 13.3% at end-June.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Q3 2024 Market Review

commentary: Prime Grade A office rent (Central, Hong Kong Island) at HKD 90.5 psf/month in Q4 2024. Vacancy was 13.6% market-wide. Overall Grade A rents declined 7.9% for full-year 2024. Central's vacancy rose significantly due to new supply completions.
source: Knight Frank Asia Pacific Q4 2024 Office Highlights

commentary: Overall Grade A office vacancy rose to 13.1% in 2024, a 25-year high. Market-wide rents declined 8.6% for full year, with Central experiencing a 12.0% drop due to competition from new supply. JLL expected overall rents to decline a further 5–10% in 2025. High Street retail rents increased 1.3% for the year while Prime shopping centre rents decreased 2.3%.
source: JLL Hong Kong Real Estate Market Outlook 2025

commentary: Overall Grade A office rents fell 7.9% in full-year 2024, with a forecasted further 9% decline in 2025. High-street shop rents rose 3.1% in 2024. Warehouse rents fell 5.5% for the year. Savills expected rents to drop further by 5–10% in 2025. Vacancy remained elevated market-wide.
source: Savills Hong Kong Research Market Update Q4 2024

commentary: Prime Grade A office rent (Central, Hong Kong Island) at HKD 89.9 psf/month in Q1 2025, with vacancy at 13.6%. Prime rents fell 0.9% QoQ in Q1 2025, a steeper decline than the 0.4% drop in Q4 2024. The market continued to grapple with ample supply pipeline while demand remained concentrated in premium-grade buildings.
source: Knight Frank Asia Pacific Q1 2025 Office Highlights

commentary: Overall Grade A office vacancy rose to 13.7% in Q1 2025, with Kowloon East increasing to 21.3%. Rents declined 1.3% QoQ overall, with Hong Kong East recording the steepest drop at -3.4%. Core districts Central and Tsimshatsui saw modest improvements in occupancy. JLL maintained a -5% to -10% full-year 2025 rent forecast.
source: JLL Hong Kong Q1 2025 Preliminary Market Summary

commentary: Overall Central net effective rent stood at HKD 86.5 psf/month in Q2 2025, down 1.3% QoQ and 6.9% YoY. Premium Central commanded HKD 101.1 psf/month (-0.7% QoQ, -6.6% YoY). Vacancy in Central was 13.5%. Jane Street's significant pre-commitment at Harbourfront Site 3 (223,000 sq ft) was a positive signal for Central landlords. Flight-to-quality remains the dominant theme.
source: Knight Frank Hong Kong Market Report Q2 2025

commentary: Overall vacancy fell marginally by 0.1 ppt to 17.4% in Q2 2025. Overall rents dropped 0.6% QoQ and 2.8% YTD. Rents in Central remained stable QoQ — the only major submarket without a decline in Q2. Greater Central reported 155,400 sq ft net absorption, strongest half-year total since H2 2015, supported by major pre-commitment from Jane Street. Industrial warehouse vacancy rose to 10.3%.
source: CBRE Hong Kong H1 2025 Market Review

commentary: Overall Central net effective rent was HKD 85.7 psf/month in Q3 2025, down 1.0% QoQ and 5.9% YoY. Premium Central held at HKD 101.3 psf/month (+0.2% QoQ). Total Grade A vacancy stood at 14.5% with take-up of +311,437 sq ft. Financial sector demand for premium Central Grade A drove positive absorption; non-core offices faced heightened competitive pressure.
source: Knight Frank Hong Kong Market Report Q3 2025

commentary: Citywide net absorption reached 691,800 sq ft in Q3 2025, the highest quarterly total since Q3 2018, with all major submarkets recording positive absorption for the first time since Q2 2015. Vacancy fell 0.3 ppt to 17.1%, the largest quarterly decline since Q3 2018. Rents declined 0.7% QoQ overall (YTD -3.4%), though Greater Tsim Sha Tsui rents held firm. Warehouse vacancy rose to a record 11.8%.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Q3 2025 Market Review

commentary: Total net absorption rebounded 137.5% QoQ to 646,000 sq ft in Q3 2025. Overall office vacancy declined from 13.6% in June to 13.4% in September. Central and Kowloon East vacancy rates fell 0.8 ppt each. Overall office rents declined 0.8% QoQ; Central rents fell only 0.3%. Industrial prime warehouse rents declined 2.1% in Q3 2025 (after -2.4% in Q2); vacancy rose to 9.3%.
source: JLL Hong Kong Q3 2025 Preliminary Market Summary

commentary: Overall Central net effective rent rose to HKD 88.1 psf/month in Q4 2025 (+2.0% QoQ, -2.7% YoY). Premium Central reached HKD 105.8 psf/month (+2.9% QoQ, +3.0% YoY) — first positive YoY growth in years. Total Grade A vacancy was 15.6%, take-up +880,125 sq ft. Banking, finance and law firms drove premium Central demand; Traditional Central and peripheral markets continued to underperform.
source: Knight Frank Hong Kong Market Report Q4 2025

commentary: Overall rents edged up 0.6% QoQ in Q4 2025 — first growth since Q2 2019. Central rents rose 3.7% QoQ and Tsim Sha Tsui +1.7% QoQ. For full-year 2025, overall rents contracted 2.9% YoY (smallest full-year decline since 2019); Central rents were broadly flat (-0.1%). Citywide vacancy rose to 17.3%; Central vacancy declined for a fourth consecutive quarter to 11.1%. Warehouse vacancy reached a record 13% (+1.3 ppt QoQ); warehouse rents fell 2.0% QoQ (full-year -8.4%).
source: CBRE Hong Kong Commercial Real Estate Market Outlook 2026

commentary: Hong Kong's Grade A office market turned a corner in Q4 2025, with Central and Tsimshatsui leading the rebound posting rental growth of 0.5% and 0.2% respectively in H2 2025. Overall rents declined 1.5% for full-year 2025, led by a 10% drop in Hong Kong East while Central saw only a mild 0.4% decrease. Central vacancy rate fell to 10.9% in H2 2025. Prime warehouse vacancy reached a decade-high of 10.1% at end-2025 with rents down 7.2%.
source: JLL 2026: Hong Kong's office and housing markets lead recovery

commentary: Overall Grade A office vacancy rose to 15.5% in December 2025, up 0.9 ppt YoY, but Central vacancy declined 1.9 ppt to 11.3%, reinforcing Central's safe haven status. Average rents in Central held at approximately HKD 85 psf/month. Premium Grade A buildings in Central (Two IFC, Chater House, The Henderson) maintained occupancy above 88%. Savills forecasts premium office rents in Central and Tsim Sha Tsui to rise 5–7% in 2026.
source: Savills Hong Kong Office Market 2025 Review (via Real Estate Asia)

commentary: Overall Central net effective rent reached HKD 92.8 psf/month in Q1 2026 (+5.4% QoQ, +5.9% YoY). Premium Central surged to HKD 111.2 psf/month (+5.1% QoQ, +9.2% YoY). Total Grade A vacancy stood at 14.5%, take-up +563,633 sq ft. JP Morgan Chase committed to 246,000 sq ft at Artist Square Tower in West Kowloon. Traditional Central (+5.7% QoQ) and Admiralty (+2.6% QoQ) also strengthened.
source: Knight Frank Hong Kong Market Report Q1 2026

commentary: Overall Grade A office rents rose 1.6% QoQ in Q1 2026 — the strongest growth since Q3 2018. Central rents surged 5.9% QoQ; Grade A1 buildings in Central rose 12.1% QoQ, the fastest rental growth since Q3 2010. Citywide vacancy declined 0.4 ppt to 16.8%, the biggest quarterly decline since Q2 2015. New leasing volume was 682,800 sq ft (+17.4% YoY). Industrial warehouse vacancy narrowed 0.3 ppt to 12.8% but rents fell 1.2% QoQ (9th consecutive quarterly decline).
source: CBRE Hong Kong Q1 2026 Market Review

commentary: Industrial warehouse vacancy rose to 7.9% in Q2 2024, up sharply from 5.5% in Q1 2024. CBRE had expected a mild correction in H1 2024 due to sluggish leasing demand and rising shadow space. Rents declined as landlords placed greater emphasis on occupancy over maximising income.
source: CBRE Hong Kong H1 2024 Market Review

commentary: Warehouse vacancy rose to 8.4% in Q3 2024 (from 7.9% at end-Q2). Warehouse rents declined 1.0% QoQ. Landlords prioritised keeping occupancy rates high rather than maximising rental income.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Q3 2024 Market Review

commentary: Warehouse rents fell 1.1% QoQ in Q4 2024, bringing the full-year rental decline to -4.6% YoY — the sharpest annual fall since 2020. Landlords continued prioritising occupancy over rental income. Overall warehouse rents contracted 5.5% for full-year 2024 with a forecasted further 4% decline in 2025.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Industrial Q4 2024 Figures

commentary: Prolonged and elevated vacancy contributed to a 2.1% QoQ decline in warehouse rents in Q1 2025, marking a fifth consecutive quarterly drop. Landlords continued to soften leasing terms to maintain occupancy amid ongoing supply-demand imbalance.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Industrial Q1 2025 Figures

commentary: Warehouse vacancy increased to 10.3% by end of Q2 2025 (+0.4 ppt QoQ). Rents fell 0.8% QoQ in Q2 2025, the sixth consecutive quarterly drop, bringing the YTD decline to 2.9%. Leasing activity was largely driven by relocations with potential downsizing. Notable large deals included 100,000 sq ft at Cainiao Smart Gateway and 92,000 sq ft at China Merchants Logistics Centre.
source: CBRE Hong Kong H1 2025 Market Review

commentary: Prime warehouse vacancy rate rose to 9.1% in Q2 2025. Prime warehouse rents declined 2.4% QoQ. Geopolitical tensions and uncertain trade policies in H1 2025 prompted a more cautious approach from occupiers. Limited new commitments drove the vacancy increase.
source: JLL Hong Kong H1 2025 Market Review

commentary: Modern logistics prime rent declined to HKD 16.4 psf/month in Q3 2025 (-2.0% QoQ, -6.7% YoY). Modern logistics vacancy rose to 13.3% (+0.6 ppt QoQ). General industrial rents averaged HKD 12.2 psf/month (-1.6% QoQ, -4.6% YoY) with vacancy at 8.5%. Primary leasing activity was dominated by renewals; warehouse landlords offered unprecedented rent-free periods to attract tenants.
source: Knight Frank Hong Kong Industrial Summary Q3 2025

commentary: Prime warehouse vacancy rose to 9.3% in Q3 2025 from 9.1% in Q2 2025. Prime warehouse rents declined 2.1% QoQ. Local supply chain and trading firms remained weak tenants; PRC firms expanding into Hong Kong provided some demand. Structural headwinds from route reconfiguration and retailer consolidation continued.
source: JLL Hong Kong Q3 2025 Preliminary Market Summary

commentary: Warehouse vacancy reached a record high of 13.0% in Q4 2025 (+1.3 ppt QoQ). Warehouse rents fell 2.0% QoQ, bringing the full-year 2025 decline to -8.4% — the worst year since peak. Total contraction from Q4 2023 peak reached -12.7%. Leasing volume improved 55% QoQ to 1.1 million sq ft in Q4. Negative yield carry persisted across commercial property sectors.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Industrial Q4 2025 Figures

commentary: Prime warehouse vacancy reached a decade-high of 10.1% at end-2025. Prime warehouse rents declined 7.2% for full-year 2025. Capital values for prime warehouses fell 10.3% in 2025. Structural changes including greater use of routes bypassing Hong Kong, retailer consolidation, and global supply chain reconfiguration are key headwinds. JLL forecasts further 5–10% decline in rents and capital values in 2026.
source: JLL 2026: Hong Kong's office and housing markets lead recovery

commentary: Warehouse vacancy narrowed 0.3 ppt QoQ to 12.8% in Q1 2026 — positive net absorption of 135,800 sq ft marking the end of four consecutive quarters of net withdrawal. However, warehouse rents fell a further 1.2% QoQ as landlords cut rates to improve occupancy. This was the ninth consecutive quarterly rental decline, with total contraction from Q4 2023 peak reaching -13.7%. New leasing volume rose 17.4% YoY with electronics-sector logistics companies accounting for 31%.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Q1 2026 Market Review

commentary: Prime warehouse vacancy hit 10.5% in Q1 2026, with slight vacancy improvement from Q4 2025 levels. JLL noted logistics demand remains structurally challenged but emerging electronics demand and pre-leasing for high-spec facilities provide selective support. Rents expected to fall a further 5–10% in 2026 per December 2025 forecast.
source: JLL Hong Kong Industrial Market Dynamics Q1 2026

commentary: High street shop vacancy across four core retail districts was 6.8% in Q2 2024, unchanged from end-Q1. Overall high street rents increased 1.0% QoQ in Q3 2024. Total retail sales in July 2024 fell 11.8% YoY, reflecting weak consumer sentiment. Retail leasing was resilient in core districts despite soft macro backdrop.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Q3 2024 Market Review

commentary: High street shop rents increased 1.0% QoQ in Q3 2024 while Prime Shopping Mall rents rose 2.0% QoQ. Vacancy for high street shops in core districts held at 6.8%. Overall high-street shop rents increased 3.1% for full-year 2024.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Q3 2024 Market Review

commentary: High Street shop vacancy rate was 10.5% at end-2024 (slightly decreased from 11.6% at end-2023). Prime shopping centre vacancy stood at 8.9%. Rental values of High Street shops increased 1.3% for full-year 2024; Prime shopping centres decreased 2.3% for the year. JLL expected retail rents to decline 0–5% in 2025.
source: JLL Hong Kong Real Estate Market Outlook 2025

commentary: High-street shop rents rose 3.1% for full-year 2024, showing resilience despite weak retail sales. Savills forecasted high-street rents to grow mildly by 0–5% in 2025 and noted core prime street shops approaching the bottom of the rental cycle.
source: Savills Hong Kong Research Market Update Q4 2024

commentary: Net effective rent for overall prime shopping centre and high street retail markets stood at HKD 206 psf/month in Q2 2025, down 3.9% YoY. Rent downtrend persisted amid retailer cost-consciousness. Overall Prime shopping centre rents declined 3.1% QoQ while Premium Prime declined 2.7%. High street vacancy edged up to 10.5% by end-June; Prime shopping centre vacancy also rose to 10.5% in H1 2025.
source: JLL Hong Kong Retail Market Q2 2025 Insights (via Scribd)

commentary: Core retail district vacancy declined 0.7 ppt to 7.1% in Q2 2025. Central retail vacancy remained stable at 6.6%. Rents increased 0.9% QoQ in Q2 (matching Q1 pace), bringing H1 2025 growth to 1.9% — driven by lower vacancy in core districts and mild demand. Retail sales rose 2.4% YoY in May (first positive month in 14 months), supported by mainland Golden Week visitors.
source: CBRE Hong Kong H1 2025 Market Review

commentary: High Street shop rents declined 1.4% QoQ in Q3 2025, standing 52.6% below the Q2 2019 peak. Prime Shopping Centre rents fell 3.3% QoQ; Premium Prime Shopping Centre rents declined 3.8% QoQ. High street vacancy improved to 9.7% by end of Q3 (from 10.7% in Q2). Causeway Bay, Central and Tsimshatsui core streets recorded QoQ declines within 1%.
source: JLL Hong Kong Q3 2025 Preliminary Market Summary

commentary: Retail vacancy edged up 0.9 ppt QoQ to 8.0% in Q3 2025; Central retail was the only district reporting a slight vacancy decrease. Positive leasing activity concentrated in core streets. High-spec retail units along prime thoroughfares in Central and Causeway Bay continued to attract quality F&B and luxury brands.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Q3 2025 Market Review

commentary: Prime street shop rents are expected to grow 5–10% in 2026, reflecting improving sentiment. Key Q4 2025 retail lettings included: Longbridge Securities at 58 Russell Street, Causeway Bay at HKD 164 psf/month; Lactose at 12 Pedder Street, Central at HKD 200 psf/month; Insta360 at 22-36 Paterson Street, Causeway Bay at HKD 250 psf/month. Retail landscape remains polarised between luxury and budget segments.
source: Knight Frank Hong Kong Market Report Q4 2025

commentary: Vacancy rate for high street shops in four core retail districts fell 2.2 ppt to 5.8% in Q4 2025 — the lowest since Q4 2019. Rents increased 0.6% QoQ in Q4, bringing full-year 2025 growth to 2.9%. Retail leasing maintained active momentum driven by tourism rebound and robust F&B demand throughout 2025.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Commercial Real Estate Market Outlook 2026

commentary: High Street shop rents fell 7.7% for full-year 2025 while regular shopping mall base rents fell 9.1% and high-end malls 9.7%. Capital values for High Street shops plunged 17.1% in 2025. JLL forecasts high street rents to soften 0–5% in 2026; prime shopping centre rents face steeper pressure of 5–10% decline. Capital to concentrate on assets offering 6–7% initial yields.
source: JLL 2026: Hong Kong's office and housing markets lead recovery

commentary: Core prime street shop rents rose 1.1% QoQ in Q4 2025. Total retail sales reached HKD 380.46 billion in 2025. Savills' Jack Tong forecast prime street shop rents to remain broadly stable or grow mildly by up to 5% in 2026, as rental levels approach the bottom of the cycle. Retail cap rates cited by Colliers ranged from 3.25% to 5.10% in Q4 2025.
source: Savills Hong Kong Retail Market Outlook 2026 (via The Standard)

commentary: High street shop vacancy in core retail districts rose 1.0 ppt QoQ to 6.8% in Q1 2026, but remains the second-lowest figure since Q1 2024. Rents for high street shops in core retail districts increased 0.9% QoQ — the 15th consecutive quarterly increase. Jan-Feb 2026 retail sales grew 11.8% YoY to HKD 72.4 billion, supported by a 18.4% rise in visitor arrivals.
source: CBRE Hong Kong Q1 2026 Market Review

commentary: JLL expects capital to concentrate on retail assets offering 6–7% initial yields in 2026, reflecting the gap required to make investment economics work amid negative rental reversions. Prime shopping centre rents projected to fall 5–10% in 2026 while high street rents face 0–5% softening. Retail sales remained resilient with +11.8% YoY growth in Jan-Feb 2026.
source: JLL Hong Kong Retail Market Dynamics Q1 2026 / Prime retail rents set to slide

commentary: Residential leasing market rose 0.2% MoM in November and 4.3% YTD as of Q4 2025. Luxury leasing rose 11.2% YoY by March 2026. Mass residential price index rose 1.13% YoY in October 2025, the first consecutive YoY gains in 43 months. Knight Frank luxury residential rent forecast for 2025 was 0% to +3%; mass market +3% to +5%.
source: Knight Frank Hong Kong Market Report Q4 2025 / Q1 2026
